insight: Three customer groups separate who orders again on a later, held-out quarter: repeat rates run from 35% (lapsed infrequent low-value) to 89% (recent frequent high-value).
evidence: S1 segment-score AUC 0.712 (95% CI 0.694-0.727); stability ARI p05 0.882

insight: A simple RFM quintile rule is not distinguishable from the k-means segments and is simpler to run, so the rule is the practical choice for operations.
evidence: S2 k-means minus rule -0.005 (95% CI -0.014 to +0.004), not distinguishable from 0; rule AUC 0.717 (95% CI 0.700-0.733)

insight: Segments carry information beyond how recently a customer last ordered, though the gain is small.
evidence: S4 recency + segments minus recency +0.033 (95% CI +0.027 to +0.040), positive (CI excludes 0); recency-only AUC 0.685 (95% CI 0.666-0.703)

insight: Post hoc, descriptive: 94% of the model's top 500 ordered again, and 83% of 500 customers picked at random from the top RFM group. This is not a paired test and does not show that the model ranks better than the rule.
Inside each RFM group the model still orders customers above chance, but less well in the low and middle groups. Scores order customers; they are not probabilities.
evidence: within top RFM group 0.742 (0.705-0.778); middle group 0.590 (0.557-0.626); calibration slope 1.22 fails P2 (results.json)
